units.name: mavsdk-session-core
units.role: The front door: Mavsdk/System/ServerComponent objects and the plugin base classes everything else plugs into.
units.description: This is the heart of the MAVSDK library: the objects an application actually holds onto. Mavsdk is the object you create to start using the library, it opens connections (UDP/TCP/serial) to vehicles, discovers them, and hands out System objects, one per connected vehicle or ground station. ServerComponent is the mirror image: it represents a virtual component (e.g. a companion computer or camera) that MAVSDK itself impersonates on the network. Every feature of MAVSDK is implemented as a plugin constructed from a System (client side) or a ServerComponent (server side); this unit defines the base classes every one of those plugins derives from, the Handle mechanism used to unsubscribe from callbacks, and a handful of small public value types (Autopilot, CompatibilityMode, Vehicle, Geometry, math/base64 helpers) with no better home. It must never let a plugin outlive the System/ServerComponent that owns it, and must always marshal callbacks onto the caller's own thread rather than the network I/O thread.

units.name: mavlink-transport-io
units.role: Opens UDP/TCP/serial connections, turns bytes into MAVLink frames and back, with no protocol-level meaning attached.
units.description: This is the part of MAVSDK that actually pushes and pulls raw bytes over the wire to reach a drone: opening UDP sockets, TCP client/server sockets, and serial ports, reading whatever arrives and reassembling it into MAVLink message frames, and queuing outgoing MAVLink messages without losing data on a stalled link. It also includes small, low-level building blocks these connections share: a pool of MAVLink parsing channels, hostname-to-IP lookup, and a handful of cross-cutting utilities (logging, clock access, string helpers, a generic ring buffer) with no better home. This unit does not know what any MAVLink message means; it only knows how to get bytes to and from a socket or port and hand parsed frames to whoever registered a callback. It must never silently drop a partially-received frame without giving the parser a chance to resync.

entrypoints.name: Connection

units.name: mavlink-protocol-dispatch
units.role: The rules of a MAVLink conversation: message routing, command ack/retry, heartbeats, timers, and the Sender contract.
units.description: This is the part of MAVSDK that understands the rules of a MAVLink conversation once bytes have already been turned into messages: which message goes to which piece of code that asked for it, what it means to send a command and wait for the vehicle to acknowledge it (including retrying if it does not answer in time), how to reassemble a status text message that arrived in several pieces, how to keep sending and checking heartbeats safely, how to measure round-trip time with the autopilot's clock, and the generic one-shot and repeating timers all of this timing logic is built on. It also defines Sender, the small abstract contract other units use to hand a finished MAVLink message off to be transmitted, without knowing about sockets. It sits between raw transport and individual feature plugins, which rely on it to talk to a vehicle reliably without each reinventing command retries or message routing. It must never report a command as acknowledged before the vehicle actually confirms it.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkMessageHandler

entrypoints.name: MavlinkCommandSender

entrypoints.name: MavlinkCommandReceiver

entrypoints.name: MavlinkRequestMessage

entrypoints.name: MavlinkStatustextHandler

entrypoints.name: TimeoutHandler

entrypoints.name: CallEveryHandler

entrypoints.name: Sender

units.name: mavlink-parameter-protocol
units.role: The MAVLink parameter protocol: read/write named vehicle settings reliably, with retries and a local cache.
units.description: This unit implements the MAVLink parameter protocol, the standard way a ground-station or companion computer reads and writes a drone's named configuration settings over an unreliable link. On the requesting side it turns a simple get/set call into the right sequence of PARAM_REQUEST_READ/PARAM_SET/PARAM_VALUE (or extended, string-capable PARAM_EXT_*) messages, retries them if no answer comes in time, and keeps a local cache so fetching all parameters is not repeated. On the answering side it keeps the authoritative set of parameters, answers requests from any number of remote clients, and broadcasts a value whenever it changes. A ParamValue type represents a parameter's value together with its exact wire type so conversions are always done correctly. It must never report a set-parameter as successful before the vehicle echoes back the new value.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkParameterClient
entrypoints.plain: Get/set a vehicle parameter, or fetch all of them, with retries.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkParameterServer
entrypoints.plain: Serve/store parameters and answer remote read/write/list requests.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkParameterSubscription
entrypoints.plain: Get notified whenever a given parameter's value changes.

entrypoints.name: ParamValue

units.name: mavlink-ftp-protocol
units.role: MAVLink-FTP: chunked file transfer, directory listing and CRC verification between client and vehicle.
units.description: This unit implements MAVLink's file-transfer protocol, the mechanism drones and companion software use to browse, upload, download, rename and delete files on a vehicle's onboard storage over a MAVLink link. It defines both sides: a client that requests transfers, retries lost packets, verifies file integrity with checksums, and writes downloaded data to local files; and a server that answers those requests by reading, writing and listing files under a configured root directory and streaming large downloads in bursts. Other parts of MAVSDK call into this unit whenever they need to move a file to or from a drone. It must never report a download as complete unless the checksum of the assembled local file matches what the vehicle reported.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkFtpClient
entrypoints.plain: Download, upload, list, create, remove and rename files on the vehicle.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkFtpServer
entrypoints.plain: Serve a local directory to remote MAVLink-FTP clients.

entrypoints.name: Crc32
entrypoints.plain: Compute a CRC32 checksum, used to verify file integrity after transfer.

effects.description: Reads/writes local files during upload/download and computes local file CRC32; server creates/removes/renames files and directories under its configured root.
Reads MAVSDK_FTP_DEBUGGING to enable verbose protocol logging.
Paces burst-read packet transmission and times out stalled transfers/retries.

units.name: mavlink-mission-transfer
units.role: Reliably upload/download an ordered list of mission items to/from a vehicle over MAVLink.
units.description: This code implements the back-and-forth conversation MAVSDK has with a drone to reliably send or fetch an ordered list of mission waypoints. Because the radio link can drop or reorder messages, the protocol counts the items, requests them one at a time, acknowledges receipt, and retries with a timeout if a step is not answered in time. This unit only knows the mechanics of that handshake, it does not know or care what a waypoint means to a flight plan, a geofence, or a rally point; that meaning is added by the plugins that call into it. It must never report an upload or download as finished before every item has been individually accounted for.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkMissionTransferClient
entrypoints.plain: Upload, download, clear, or set the current item of a mission item list.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkMissionTransferServer
entrypoints.plain: Accept an incoming mission upload, or serve stored items to a requesting client.

effects.description: Schedules and refreshes retry/timeout deadlines for every outstanding upload/download/clear/set-current request.

units.name: http-download-utility
units.role: Fetch a URL's content (to memory or to a file) over HTTP/HTTPS on a background thread.
units.description: This is a small, self-contained toolbox for fetching things from the internet over HTTP/HTTPS. Given a web address, it can either read the content into memory as text or save it to a file on disk, optionally reporting download progress along the way. It does the actual network work in a background thread so callers do not have to wait or manage networking details themselves. It has no knowledge of drones, flight, or the MAVLink protocol, it is purely a generic 'go get this URL' helper other parts of the program plug into. It must never leave a partially-written file at the caller's requested path after a failed download.

entrypoints.name: HttpLoader
entrypoints.plain: Queue a URL to be downloaded to memory or a file, with progress/completion callbacks.

effects.description: Performs HTTP/HTTPS GET requests via libcurl, with TLS verification enabled and redirects followed.
Opens/writes/removes a local file when downloading to a path, and reads a file's size from disk.
Runs a dedicated background thread that pulls queued download jobs off an internal queue.

units.name: core-cache-utilities
units.role: Local caching and decompression for definition files (camera XML, component metadata) fetched from a vehicle or the network.
units.description: A small shared toolkit for caching downloaded definition files locally: given a URL or piece of content, decide where a copy should live in a local cache directory so it is not re-downloaded unchanged, and decompress .xz-compressed files. Used by any plugin that fetches static description data, such as camera settings XML or component metadata, and wants to keep a local copy rather than re-fetching it every time. It must never serve a stale cached file when the vehicle reports the content has changed.

entrypoints.name: FileCache

entrypoints.name: get_cache_directory

entrypoints.name: InflateLZMA
entrypoints.plain: Decompress an .xz-compressed file that was downloaded.

effects.description: Reads/writes a local cache directory and temp download paths, creating directories as needed.

units.name: vehicle-command-plugins
units.role: Direct real-time vehicle commanding: arm/takeoff/land/RTL, offboard setpoint streaming, and manual stick input.
units.description: This unit lets a ground-control application directly command a drone's motion and behaviour in real time: arming/disarming, taking off, landing, returning home and similar one-shot actions; continuously streaming attitude, position or velocity setpoints while the vehicle flies under external guidance; forwarding raw joystick input; and, for code playing the role of the vehicle itself, listening for and answering those same requests. Setpoints must never be sent to a vehicle that has not been told to expect them, and setpoint streaming must auto-stop if the vehicle's heartbeat stops confirming offboard mode.

entrypoints.name: ActionServer

Action::set_gps_global_origin blocks with a timeout while waiting for a GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN echo.

units.name: raw-mavlink-plugins
units.role: Escape hatches: send/receive arbitrary MAVLink messages, or a raw shell command to the vehicle's companion computer.
units.description: This unit is the SDK's set of break-glass escape hatches for talking to a drone when none of MAVSDK's typed feature APIs cover what is needed: building and sending an arbitrary MAVLink message by name and receiving any incoming message, including loading new message definitions at runtime from XML; an older deprecated raw-message passthrough kept for backward compatibility; and forwarding an arbitrary shell command line to run on the vehicle's companion computer (not the machine running MAVSDK), streaming the text response back. Because all four bypass the SDK's normal validation, they are powerful but easy to misuse and meant for advanced users and debugging.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkDirect
entrypoints.plain: Send/receive an arbitrary MAVLink message by name, including custom XML-defined ones.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkDirectServer

entrypoints.name: MavlinkPassthrough

entrypoints.name: Shell

Shell::send packages an arbitrary command-line string into MAVLink SERIAL_CONTROL messages executed by the connected vehicle's own companion-computer shell, not locally.

units.name: mission-safety-plugins
units.role: Planned autonomous flight behaviour: mission upload/run, geofences, and follow-me, plus the server-side mirror.
units.description: This unit covers the drone's pre-planned, autonomous flight behaviour: uploading a list of waypoints/actions and telling the vehicle to fly them on its own, the same at the raw MAVLink-item level, the mirror-image server side that lets a companion computer step through a mission on behalf of the vehicle, fencing off an area the drone must stay inside or outside of, and having the vehicle continuously follow a moving point. None of these plugins fly the drone directly, they only hand instructions to the autopilot and report back whether it accepted them. A mission must never be assumed running, or a fence assumed active, until the corresponding upload/start call has actually returned success from the vehicle.

entrypoints.name: Mission
entrypoints.plain: Upload, start, pause, download and clear a typed waypoint mission.

entrypoints.name: MissionRaw

entrypoints.name: MissionRawServer

entrypoints.name: Geofence
entrypoints.plain: Upload, download and clear geofence boundaries.

entrypoints.name: FollowMe
entrypoints.plain: Start/stop the vehicle following a continuously-updated target location.

effects.description: MissionRaw::import_qgroundcontrol_mission / import_mission_planner_mission open and read plan files from disk.
FollowMe periodically re-sends the target's position to the vehicle on a timer while active.

units.name: telemetry-sensing-plugins
units.role: Passive observation of vehicle/environment state: telemetry, ADS-B, mocap, RTK corrections, and structured events.
units.description: This unit covers passively observing vehicle/environment state rather than commanding it: streaming vehicle telemetry such as position, battery and attitude to a client, or accepting it from a companion computer; ADS-B traffic of nearby aircraft; motion-capture pose input for indoor navigation; RTK GPS correction data; a generic structured pub/sub event and health/arming-check bus; and a small server-side utility for sending free-text status messages. None of these plugins command the vehicle. Cached telemetry values must never be reported to a subscriber before the underlying MAVLink message has actually been fully received and parsed.

entrypoints.name: Telemetry
entrypoints.plain: Subscribe to or poll live vehicle state: position, battery, attitude, GPS, flight mode, health.

entrypoints.name: TelemetryServer
entrypoints.plain: Publish vehicle telemetry as if this were the vehicle.

entrypoints.name: Transponder
entrypoints.plain: Subscribe to nearby ADS-B traffic.

entrypoints.name: Mocap

entrypoints.name: Rtk

entrypoints.name: Events
entrypoints.plain: Subscribe to structured events and health/arming-check reports.

entrypoints.name: ServerUtility
entrypoints.plain: Send a free-text status message to the ground station.

effects.description: Telemetry re-requests the home position every 2s on a timer; Mocap/Rtk stamp outgoing messages with the autopilot's time source.

units.name: camera-gimbal-plugins
units.role: Control the payload camera and the gimbal that points it, plus the server-side camera-emulation counterpart.
units.description: This unit is the drone's eyes and neck: it lets an application control the payload camera (take a photo, record video, change zoom/focus/settings) and the gimbal that aims it, and lets a companion computer answer those same requests as if it were the camera itself. It does not do the actual image capture or motor control, it translates between friendly function calls and the vehicle's MAVLink camera/gimbal protocol messages, and can download/cache a camera's XML settings-description file from the vehicle or the network. It must never report a photo or video capture as started before the vehicle actually confirms it.

entrypoints.plain: Take photos, record video, change settings, track a point/rectangle.

entrypoints.name: CameraServer
entrypoints.plain: Answer camera requests as if this were the camera.

entrypoints.name: Gimbal

Reads/writes a local cache and temp download directory for camera-definition XML files; tests read bundled XML fixtures.
Reads MAVSDK_CAMERA_DEBUGGING to enable extra debug logging.
Schedules periodic polling (e.g. capture-info/status requests) on a timer.

units.name: file-transfer-plugins
units.role: Move files and file-like metadata between client and vehicle: FTP, log download/streaming, component metadata.
units.description: This unit moves files or file-like metadata between client and vehicle: generic FTP-style file access; downloading flight logs; streaming a currently-recording log in real time; and describing/discovering a component's metadata such as its parameter and event definitions, for both the requesting and the publishing side. It must never report a downloaded file as complete before every chunk has been received and, where the protocol provides one, its checksum verified.

entrypoints.name: Ftp
entrypoints.plain: Download, upload, list, create, remove, rename files on the vehicle.

entrypoints.name: FtpServer
entrypoints.plain: Serve a local directory to remote FTP clients.

entrypoints.name: LogFiles
entrypoints.plain: List and download past flight logs stored on the vehicle.

entrypoints.name: LogStreaming
entrypoints.plain: Watch a log file being written in real time while the vehicle flies.

units.name: vehicle-config-plugins
units.role: Vehicle settings, identity and small attached-accessory control: params, calibration, info, failure injection, arm gating, tune/winch/gripper.
units.description: This unit is the drone's settings-and-utility toolbox rather than its flight controls: reading and writing low-level configuration values, walking through sensor calibration, asking the vehicle who it is and what firmware it runs, deliberately breaking a subsystem for safety testing, deciding whether to grant permission for a vehicle to arm, playing a tune on the buzzer, and operating an attached winch or gripper. None of these features fly the vehicle; they configure it, describe it, test it, gate its arming, or operate small attached accessories. It must never report a parameter as written before the vehicle echoes the new value back.

entrypoints.name: Param
entrypoints.plain: Get/set the vehicle's named configuration values.

entrypoints.name: ParamServer
entrypoints.plain: Answer parameter read/write/list requests as if this were the vehicle.

entrypoints.name: Calibration
entrypoints.plain: Walk through gyro/accelerometer/magnetometer/level-horizon/gimbal calibration.

units.name: mavsdk-grpc-server
units.role: Wraps the whole MAVSDK plugin library behind a gRPC server so other-language clients can drive a vehicle over the network.
units.description: mavsdk_server is a translator program that sits between a running drone connection and other programming languages. The core MAVSDK library and its drone-control features are written in C++; this wraps that library and exposes every feature as a network service (gRPC), so a Python, Swift, Java/Kotlin or any other client library can control a drone by sending network requests instead of linking C++ code. It contains one hand-written adapter per feature area translating between a plugin's C++ API and its gRPC service, plus generated glue code implementing the wire message formats. It can run as a standalone executable or be embedded as a library in another application. It must never let a gRPC request block the server from answering unrelated requests on other services.

entrypoints.name: MavsdkServer
entrypoints.plain: Start/connect/stop a gRPC server exposing every enabled MAVSDK plugin as a network service.

effects.description: Opens an insecure gRPC (HTTP/2) server socket on 0.0.0.0:<port> and registers every enabled plugin's RPC service on it.
Delegates to Mavsdk::add_any_connection() to open the underlying MAVLink UDP/TCP/serial connection to the vehicle.
Blocks the calling thread in grpc::Server::Wait(); parses argv for connection URL, port, sysid/compid, heartbeat-watchdog timeout.

violations_observed.note: Plugin impls reach into SystemImpl/ServerComponentImpl accessor methods (e.g. send_command_async, register_mavlink_message_handler) that are private implementation detail of mavsdk-session-core rather than a formally exposed entrypoint; this manifest curates a small class-level entrypoint per unit for tractability, so many such fine-grained accessor calls are not individually enumerated as depends_on edges.

camera_impl.cpp downloads camera definition files via HttpLoader/FileCache (declared), but some plugins across the codebase also reach MavlinkFtpClient indirectly through SystemImpl for related downloads without it being declared as a direct dependency edge on every consuming unit; flagged as an area where the curated entrypoint list is a simplification of the true call graph.
